svg.text: No races by construction — who writes what, and how each kind of data crosses between the threads
Rule: each world has ONE writer. The UI reads only its own world A; the simulation reads only S. Every crossing below uses one of the mechanisms shown — and only the yellow ones take a lock.
WORLD S — written ONLY by the SIM thread
(the pool writes inside the tick via per-batch buffers)
HOW IT CROSSES
WORLD A — written ONLY by the MAIN thread
(except the sync, which holds A's lock)
SIM → UI (the sync runs on the sim thread at the tick's end)
components the map, 3-D, overlays draw
TABLE COPY at the sync — a mask of types, all rows (≈1.3 ms)
the same tables in A
the selected / inspected units' components
ROW COPY at the sync — types × selected entities (µs)
their rows in A (panels, inspector)
small per-tick singletons: GlobalTime, traces
COPIED BY VALUE at the sync
their copies in A
derived maps: NetworkEntityMap
REBUILT in A from the copied ids (0.76 ms)
A's own map
changing service state: cluster cache, clock
IMMUTABLE VIEW published — one atomic reference swap (0.01 ms)
the latest view (no lock)
shared objects: terrain, geo, TKB, behaviours, navmesh
SHARED BY REFERENCE — immutable, or replaced in ONE atomic swap
the same object, old or new, never half
native memory: the road graph
LEASED — the old version lives until the last reader lets go
a lease per sync
logs: shots, detonations, edit outcomes, squad reports
FORWARDED — the new entries copied at the sync
A's own logs
events on S's bus (hits, deaths, outcomes)
FORWARDED into A's bus at the sync — each reader gets each once
A's bus
gizmo OVERLAYS (47) drawn on the sim thread
PRIMITIVE FRAME published — triple buffer, leased by the map
the map draws the latest frame
UI → SIM (the UI never writes S)
edits: move, delete, spawn, orders, rules
COMMAND — a thread-safe queue, drained at the tick's start (Input), validated; refused ⇒ the edit outcome
applied by the sim thread
drag / rotate / place
a GHOST in A every frame — the drop is ONE command
applied by the sim thread
run controls: play, pause, step, Run-to
COMMANDS — the clock lives with the simulation
applied by the sim thread
settings the sim reads (viewport, debug toggles)
RIDE WITH THE COMMANDS — copied to S once per tick
applied by the sim thread
STAYS ON ONE SIDE — never crosses
brain memory, sensors, EQS, physics, the
node frame, the orchestrator, recording
a reader on the other side asks through a command or the HTTP API (answered at a tick boundary)
selection, menus, camera, order form,
effects, panel layout — written directly

⚠ READS MUST BE READS: a managed-component read and a singleton read stop returning a writable ref / stamping the chunk (A1-2) · the 3 unsafe statics get a lock / Concurrent / Lazy · a Debug guard throws on a write to S off the sim thread
The gizmo split — 79 gizmo classes (75 registered in the editor): overlays stay with the simulation, tools move to the frame
OVERLAYS (47) — sim thread
navmesh, cover, EQS, brain debug, routes, health,
names, traces, roads, squads, missions …
Draw(view of S) → the primitive buffer
→ published once per tick (triple buffer)
→ the map draws it at the frame rate
content changes only when S ticks ⇒ no loss;
remote nodes' overlays arrive the same way
cost moved off the UI frame: ≈ 4.4–5.5 ms
MIXED (6) — split in two
EntityPresentation, NamedPoint: overlay on sim,
their PICK BOXES on main from the copied positions
TerrainBlock, Route, Designation, FireMission:
overlay on sim, SELECTION styling on main
⭐ pick boxes and the pickers move TOGETHER —
the pickers hit-test this frame's boxes (CE-259r)
the zoom-dependent sizes come from A's camera
TOOLS & UI (26) — main thread
drag, rotate, vertex / waypoint / mission editors,
measure, place / paste ghosts, pickers, RTS mode,
box select, layer panel, selection highlight, menus
input → the tool's FSM every frame → a GHOST in A
→ the commit is ONE COMMAND to S
⛔ today the drag writes SimTransform every frame
(EntityDragGizmo.cs:278) — that becomes the ghost
the gizmo MODULE itself is split too: it also runs world WRITERS (action dispatch: Delete / LoadZone, effect + wreck spawn, lifespan) — those stay in the tick
copied at the sync, under A's lock (the only lock)
published / shared — an atomic reference swap or a lease, no lock
a command — the UI's only way into S
